questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: In one district farmers refused to sell sugarcane to the only sugar mill in the area. Explain what happened to that mill, and say which sector had to depend on which.

markingPoints.description: The mill will have to shut down
This shows the secondary or industrial sector dependent on the primary
Sugarcane growing belongs to the primary sector while the sugar mill belongs to the secondary sector

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The mill will have to shut down. This is an example of the secondary or industrial sector being dependent on the primary. Farmers grow sugarcane in the primary sector and the mill manufactures sugar from it in the secondary, so the mill cannot go on without the farmers' cane.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: Garment companies in another country decided to buy no cotton from the Indian market and to import all the cotton they need from other countries. Explain what this would do to cotton cultivation in India and to the farmers who depend on it.

markingPoints.description: Indian cotton cultivation will become less profitable
The farmers may even go bankrupt
Growing cotton is primary work while the buying and manufacturing companies are secondary, and the sectors are interdependent

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Indian cotton cultivation will become less profitable, and the farmers may even go bankrupt. Cotton growing is primary work, while the companies buying the crop and manufacturing cloth from it are secondary. As the three categories of economic activities are highly interdependent, a decision taken in one sector immediately harms the other.

questions.stem: A town now has an ATM booth where customers withdraw money, an internet cafe where students go online, and a company that answers customers' calls and writes software. Explain in about 45 words why all three belong to the tertiary sector rather than to manufacturing work.

questions.stem: Ramesh takes sugarcane from farmers, presses out the juice and boils it into gur, then stores the packed gur in a godown and sells it in a weekly market. Show, step by step, which sector each of his two stages belongs to, and why the last stage is not manufacturing work.

markingPoints.description: Step 1: places pressing sugarcane and boiling it into gur in the secondary sector, since the product has to be made and not produced by nature
Step 2: states that this sector is also called the industrial sector
Step 3: places storing the gur in a godown and selling it in a weekly market in the tertiary sector
Step 4: explains that tertiary activities do not produce a good by themselves
Step 5: explains that they are an aid or a support for the production process, so the last stage is not manufacturing

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1 — Pressing sugarcane and boiling it into gur: the product is not produced by nature but has to be made, so this is secondary sector work. Step 2 — This sector is also called the industrial sector. Step 3 — Storing the gur in a godown and selling it in a market is tertiary work. Step 4 — Not manufacturing, because tertiary activities do not produce a good by themselves. Step 5 — They are an aid or a support for production and trade.

questions.stem: A factory that weaves cloth from cotton has shut down, and the farmers who grew that cotton for it now have nobody to sell to. Show, step by step, how each group is hit by what the other group does, using the sugarcane and cotton cases.

markingPoints.description: Step 1: places sugarcane and cotton growing in the primary sector and the sugar mill and cloth factory in the secondary or industrial sector
Step 2: states that economic activities grouped into three categories are highly interdependent
Step 3: explains that if the mill or factory will not buy, Indian cotton cultivation becomes less profitable and farmers may even go bankrupt
Step 4: explains that if farmers refuse to sell sugarcane, the mill will have to shut down
Step 5: concludes that a change in one sector shows up at once in the other

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1 — Farmers growing sugarcane or cotton are primary sector; the sugar mill and cloth factory that buy their crop are secondary or industrial. Step 2 — The three categories of economic activities are highly interdependent. Step 3 — If the mill or factory will not buy, Indian cotton cultivation becomes less profitable and farmers may even go bankrupt. Step 4 — If farmers refuse to sell sugarcane, the mill will have to shut down. Step 5 — A change in one sector thus hits the other at once.

questions.stem: In a district a hospital treats patients, a school teaches children, a shop cuts hair, a bank lends money, and an office answers customer calls and writes software for other firms. Show, step by step, how these jobs divide between the sectors, and say which of them are new services that information technology has made important.

Step 2: notes that these essential services may not directly help in the production of goods
Step 3: places a bank lending money among tertiary activities such as transport, storage, communication, banking and trade

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1 — Teachers, doctors, washermen, barbers, cobblers, lawyers and administrative and accounting work are essential services in the tertiary, or service, sector. Step 2 — They may not directly help in producing goods, yet they belong to it. Step 3 — A bank lending money is tertiary too, since borrowing money from banks helps production and trade. Step 4 — Answering calls and writing software are new services based on information technology. Step 5 — All of them generate services rather than goods.

questions.stem: Laxmi has a two-hectare plot of unirrigated land. A government scheme or a bank loan pays for a well on her family's land, so that she can irrigate the plot and take a second crop, wheat. Taking one hectare of wheat to provide employment to two people for 50 days, show step by step how many family members the second crop alone can put to work.

markingPoints.description: Step 1: notes that Laxmi has a two-hectare plot of unirrigated land and that the well lets her irrigate it
Step 2: notes that she can then take a second crop, wheat
Step 3: states that one hectare of wheat provides employment to two people for 50 days, including sowing, watering, fertiliser application and harvesting
Step 4: works out 2 hectares x 2 people = 4 people, so two more members of the family can be employed in her own field
Step 5: explains that this employment is generated within the agricultural sector itself, reducing the problem of underemployment

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1 — The well lets Laxmi irrigate her two-hectare plot. Step 2 — With water she can take a second crop, wheat. Step 3 — One hectare of wheat provides employment to two people for 50 days, counting sowing, watering, fertiliser application and harvesting. Step 4 — Two hectares therefore put 2 x 2 = 4 people to work. Step 5 — So two more members of the family can be employed in her own field, within the agricultural sector itself, reducing underemployment.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
Bhoolanpur has a single sugar mill. This season the mill asked farmers in the villages around it for more sugarcane than usual. The farmers, who had already signed an agreement with a mill in the next district, refused to sell to Bhoolanpur. Left with no cane to crush, the mill had to shut down. Cotton cultivation in the same area felt the effect as well: when companies decided to buy no cotton from the Indian market and to import all the cotton they needed from other countries, Indian cotton cultivation became less profitable and the farmers there might even go bankrupt.

Name the sector the sugar mill's work belongs to, and the sector the farmers' sugarcane growing belongs to. (ii) Why did the mill have to shut down, and what does this show about the two sectors? (iii) If the companies buy no cotton from the Indian market and import all the cotton they need, what happens to Indian cotton cultivation and to the farmers?

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) The mill is secondary, or industrial; sugarcane growing is primary. (ii) Farmers refused to sell sugarcane, so the mill had nothing to crush and shut down; the secondary sector was dependent on the primary. (iii) Indian cotton cultivation becomes less profitable and the farmers may even go bankrupt.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
Rehan's father grows cotton and sells it to a spinning mill, which weaves it into cloth. The cloth is packed and sent by truck to a godown in the city, where it waits until a wholesale trader buys it. Rehan's mother keeps the family's accounts and sometimes speaks to suppliers on the telephone. A new ATM booth has opened near their house, and Rehan uses an internet cafe to check prices before selling. The family also borrows money from a bank when the cotton crop is ready to be bought.

Sort Rehan's mother's work into sectors. (ii) Which of it is an essential service that may not directly help in producing goods? (iii) Rehan's father says his family grows, makes and sells everything itself, so it needs no service sector. Why is he wrong?

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) Keeping accounts and telephoning suppliers are tertiary activities, like transport, storage, banking and trade. (ii) Both are essential services that may not directly help in producing goods. (iii) The sectors are interdependent and tertiary work only supports production and trade, so even a family that grows and makes its own goods still needs transport, storage, communication, banking and trade.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
Nandini's town has no factory; the mill closed years ago and most people now farm, sell in the market or drive vehicles. Last year an internet cafe opened in the market, a bank put in an ATM booth, and a company started taking calls from customers all day. Some farmers now send their produce to a city depot and take a bank loan to buy seeds for the season. The town council has asked everyone to say which sector they belong to.

Put the farmer, the vehicle drivers, the internet cafe and the ATM booth into sectors. (ii) Why would a farmer who takes a bank loan be recorded in more than one sector? (iii) If the ATM booth and the internet cafe shut down, which part of the town's work stops first, and why?

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) The farmer is primary; the vehicle drivers, the internet cafe and the ATM booth are tertiary. (ii) Borrowing money from a bank is itself a tertiary service, so a farmer is primary by his farming and tertiary by the loan. (iii) Banking and communication stop first, because tertiary activities support production and trade instead of producing goods of their own.
